THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:13.06.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.1505/2015 ON THE FILE OF THE 8TH ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSE JUDGE AND 33RD ACMM, MEMBER,
MACT, BENGALURU (SCCH-5), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant being dis-satisfied with the compensation of Rs.3,25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal and also exonerating the insurer is in appeal.
2. The Tribunal has exonerated the insurer on the ground that the offending vehicle did not have the requisite permit.

It is the settled law that in case of breach of policy conditions, the insurer would still, nevertheless, have to pay compensation and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

3. In that view of the matter, the finding regarding liability is set aside and the insurer is directed to pay the compensation and thereby proceed to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

4. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation :
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
I.

PECUNIARY DAMAGES  (Special Damages)
1. Expenses relating to:
 a) To treatment, 30,000-00 hospitalization, medicines, transportation (Rs.27,904/- rounded off Rs.30,000/-)
Sri. K M Srinivas vs Sri. Tomsan Thankachan on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120167500/
2 b) Nourishing food and 15,000-00 miscellaneous expenditure 2. Loss of earnings which the injured - would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
 a) Loss of earnings during -  period of treatment  b) Loss of future earnings on 1,30,000-00  account of permanent  disability  (Rs.6,000/- x 12 x 18 x  10%= Rs.1,26,900/-, which  is rounded of Rs.1,30,000/-)
3. Future medical expenses 25,000-00 II NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES  (General Damages)
4. Damages for pain, suffering and 1,00,000-00  trauma as a consequence of the  injuries 5. Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
6. Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity) TOTAL 3,25,000-00 5.

The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body, which is just and proper and is therefore, affirmed.
6. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
7. As the claimant was aged 19 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,94,400/- (Rs.9,000/- x 12 x '18' x 10%) towards 'loss of future income'.
8.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'medical expenses and Rs.15,000/-
towards 'nourishment and miscellaneous expenses'.
In my view, the said amounts are just and proper and does not require any interference.

sentences.text: Likewise the sum of Rs.25,000/- awarded towards 'future medical expenses' and the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- awarded towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.25,000/- awarded towards 'loss of amenities' is also just and proper and is also affirmed.
10. It is noticed that though the claimant was hospitalised for about 55 days, no sum is awarded towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
In my view, it is appropriate to take laid-up-period as four months and award Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000/- x 4 months) under the said head.
11. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation :

Sl. Particulars Amount  No.
 In (Rs.)
 1. Future Medical expenses 25,000/-
 2. Pain and sufferings 1,00,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities 25,000/-
 4. Medical expenses 30,000/-
 5. Nourishment and Miscellaneous 15,000/-
 expenses  6. Loss of future income 1,94,400/-
 7. Loss of income during laid-up 36,000/-
 period
Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.4,25,400/- as against Rs.3,25,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
14. On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the same as per the terms of the award of the Tribunal.
